reason: Converting both dogfood runners to PHP produced two lessons at once: the reason that actually held (testability, not portability) and a regression caused by applying a static rule outside the scope it was earned in. Scope names the converted runners and the directory their decisions moved into, because that is where the pattern is checkable.
new: Dogfood runners orchestrate; every decision they make lives in a tested class under src/Dogfood/. Convert a shell runner for testability rather than portability - Git for Windows ships bash, so the portability argument does not hold. A static rule carries the scope it was earned in: -n belongs to validation subprocesses, not to invoking our own CLI, which needs the extensions php.ini loads.
boundary: Applies to repository dogfood runners. Git hooks stay shell, because Git invokes them directly and the portability argument is weakest there.
scope_justification: Converting both dogfood runners to PHP produced two lessons at once: the reason that actually held (testability, not portability) and a regression caused by applying a static rule outside the scope it was earned in. Scope names the converted runners and the directory their decisions moved into, because that is where the pattern is checkable.

validation_case.given: a shell runner whose decisions cannot be unit tested
validation_case.when: it is converted to PHP and the decisions stay inline in the script
validation_case.then: nothing is gained, because the conversion buys testability only if the decisions move into classes a test can call
